who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane L3 def-rest of the front-end-on-memo port, port-memo-1113
where: crates/hir-def (attrs.rs, item_tree.rs, expr_store/*, lang_item.rs, signatures.rs); crates/blaze-memo/src/keep.rs
what: The spec says owning values (Box, Arc, ArenaMap, Vec, HashMap) become `&'db T` via keep/keep_slice, but `keep` asserts `!needs_drop`, so every value holding a Vec, a Box or an Arc (item trees, stores, source maps, docs, cfg exprs, syntax values) could not be ported as written; and ids grew from 4 to 8 bytes (`Gid`) with no `to_bits`/`from_bits`, so every 32-bit id packing (item scope entries, loc size asserts, persisted id words) had to be redone by guesswork, write-only, with no compile to check the new sizes.
cost: a mid-lane redesign (`owns`, added by L1 on request), ~50 `owns` sites, and size asserts written from arithmetic, not a compiler
cause: the spec's per-site rules were written from the engine's attributes, not from the value types they apply to, and the id width change was not costed against the packings that assumed 4-byte ids
class: a mechanical port spec that does not survey the types and layouts its rules touch, so a whole class of sites is found blocked only in the lane
prevention: before a port spec is final, run a survey (rg + needs_drop of every query value type, size_of of every id-holding struct) and list the blocked classes with their decision in the spec
workaround: `#[blaze_memo::tracked(.., owns)]` on owning values; `Gid::from_bits`/`to_bits` assumed of L1; sizes recomputed by hand
